semantic_checks.claim: Real coordinate order and exact complexification
semantic_checks.result: For z : Fin 4 -> Real, X is the Euclidean Position WithLp.toLp 2 [z0,z1,z2] and T is WithLp.toLp 2 [0,0,z3]. Casting z coordinatewise before the previously proved complex slice gives exactly Sum.elim of the coordinatewise complex casts of these same X and T. No center shift, conjugation, scale, or coordinate permutation occurs.

The spectator vector has only its third coordinate nonzero. Its actual Euclidean norm equals the real norm |z3| for all z, including zero and negative z3; the proof compares nonnegative squared norms.

semantic_checks.claim: Spatial Euclidean norm and sup comparison
semantic_checks.result: The actual squared spatial norm is z0^2+z1^2+z2^2. Each of these three squares is at most the square of the plain Fin 4 Pi sup norm, giving ||X|| <= sqrt(3)*||z||. The proof uses nonnegativity before comparing squares and proves (sqrt(3))^2=3; it does not replace the Euclidean norm by the array norm.

The exact premise ||z||_sup < min(rho/sqrt(3),r) yields ||X||_Euclidean < rho and ||T||_Euclidean < r. The spatial step multiplies the strict rho/sqrt(3) bound by the positive sqrt(3); the spectator step uses |z3| <= ||z||. There is no loss of strictness or missing factor.
